title: (console-era remnant, small, visual): the bloom's ring and the image effects' blur stretch their vertical radius by 1.333 when the screen is wide and by 1.0 otherwise (BloomEffectSimple.cpp:28, ImageEffectLocalUtil.cpp:146). The radius is a fraction of the frame, so 1.333 keeps the console's shape at 16:9 only; at 21:9 and other wide shapes the blur is squashed, below 4:3 stretched.
note: Found by the inventory's pass two (docs/engine/CONSOLE-FREE.md, 11-18). Modern form: the vertical factor is the frame's aspect over 4:3 (1.333 at 16:9 as now), read from the display aspect the camera and layouts use; tests at 4:3, 16:9 and 21:9.

title: (console-era remnant, render): the depth of field keeps the console's indirect-texture lookup. The frame's depth is averaged into a half-size RGBA8 target (frame_depth.hlsl; ImageEffectLocalUtil.cpp:113-124), read back as 8 bits less 128 and moved through an indirect matrix diag(0.5*2^exp) into a 128x2 ramp texture drawn each frame from the area's distances in bytes of the window depth (DepthOfFieldBlur.cpp:99-141, dof_final.hlsl).
note: Found by the inventory's pass two (the Game/Screen whole read, 11-18, every line cited read at 6577392b5). Modern form: the final pass reads the depth buffer at full precision and computes the blur weight from the two distances (converted once from the disc's byte units); no ramp target, no 8-bit depth copy. ScreenBlurEffect.cpp:97 and FallOutFieldDraw.cpp:100 share frame_depth and move with it. The blur itself (quarter-size box) is modern already. The readall harness's Screen report did not list it.

title: (console-era remnant, resolution): the underwater camera filter warps the picture by 0.05 screen texels per indirect step (WaterCameraFilter.cpp:43-44; water_camera.hlsl: step = texel*255-128), at most about 6.4 pixels whatever the resolution: 1% of the console's 640, 0.17% at 3840, so the warp shrinks as the resolution grows and moves with dynamic resolution.
note: Found by the inventory's pass two (the Game/Screen whole read, 11-18, every line cited read at 6577392b5). Modern form: the warp as a share of the picture (0.05 per step over the authored width), the same look at every size.

title: (console-era remnant, render): the image effects hand their constants over at the console's 8-bit register precision. The bloom's eased settings are floats and are cut to bytes at every update (ImageEffectState.cpp:103-113, two of them divided by 255 again); the bloom packs threshold, two tap weights and intensity x fade into one word of four bytes (BloomEffect.cpp:61-65, BloomEffectSimple.cpp:26-35), which every renderer unpacks (for example renderer_d3d11_scene.cpp:992, :1025); the screen blur's alpha is a byte (ScreenBlurEffect.cpp:75). A fade in or out of the bloom moves in 1/255 steps.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Screen report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. The blur's depth key of 240/255 (ScreenBlurEffect.cpp:25) reads the 8-bit depth copy of P-198. Modern form: the passes take float constants written once a step (threshold, weights, intensity, alpha); the authored byte targets of the area data stay as content. Replay identical (no step reads them). 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src/render report, checked at 241395b49): the bloom's selection compares in the console's intensity copy encoding, BT.601 16-235 with the 255/256 factor rounded to 8 bits (game_bloom.hlsl:130-134; kLargestIntensity 235, game_bloom_shape.h:147-160); modern form: the threshold turned once into the linear-luminance boundary that selects the same pixels.

title: (console-era remnant, the game's bloom on Direct3D 12; one question for the owner): the normal bloom copies the frame out of the scene target (GameBloom::keep, game_bloom.cpp:345-351; copy_frame, :207-233, CopyTextureRegion), the game draws its glowing models over black into the same target, and the composite writes the kept scene back with the bloom added, or alone (restore, :564-579; :560): the console's frame copy and write-back around the glow pass. Every scene texel is clamped to 1 before the bloom, the HDR scene's too, "as the 8-bit scene target keeps it" (game_bloom.hlsl:5-6, :64-71).
note: Found by the readall harness's runtime/src/render report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the glow models draw into a target of their own as a stated pass (FRAME-MODEL 2.5), the scene stays in place and the composite only adds; on every renderer. Replay identical. Question: on HDR output keep the console's clamp (the look as made) or bloom from the unclamped energy (a change of look, not of steps)? 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src/render/d3d11 report, checked at 241395b49): Direct3D 11 does the same: GameBloom::keep copies the scene out (game_bloom_d3d11.cpp:201-205) before the glow pass and the composite writes it back. 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src/render/mtl report, checked at 241395b49): Metal trades the scene colour for the bloom texture instead of copying, but ends and reopens the scene pass where the game's stream puts the bloom (RendererMtl::game_bloom, renderer_mtl_fx.mm:72-84): on a tiled GPU a store and a load each. 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src/render/vk report, checked at 241395b49): Vulkan ends the scene pass for the game's bloom (renderer_vk_frame.cpp:2087-2090); its scale, the frame's height over kAuthoredLines, is a division by a double (:2091; frame_pass.h:36), not the integer division the report feared. Owner 11-19: bloom from the real brightness on HDR output.

title: (console-era remnant, depth and masks through colour copies): depth is copied into a half-size colour target and read back as 8-bit channels (frame_depth.hlsl:24-33); depth of field reads that copy as alpha, blue and green less 128 through an indirect matrix and a ramp's alpha (dof_final.hlsl:18-23); the screen blur compares an 8-bit depth capture with an 8-bit threshold (screen_blur.hlsl:17-20); the fall-out field's mask is recovered from that depth copy (frame_depth.hlsl:26-29) and the clip fill is masked by the screen's alpha rounded to 8 bits (clip_fill.hlsl:18-25).
note: Found by the readall harness's runtime/src/render/materials report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the passes read the scene's depth target by name (FRAME-MODEL 2.5); depth of field's blur amount in float from the focus curve; the blur's threshold turned into the host's depth encoding and compared in float; masks written by their own draws into a one-channel target or stencil, read by name. Replay identical.

title: (performance): the Gaussian blur's sigma is its width as a fraction of the picture over one texel, so its taps per pixel, ceil(3 sigma), grow with the target's size with no cap (gaussian_blur.hlsl:18-34): the pass grows with the cube of the scale.
note: Found by the readall harness's runtime/src/render/materials report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: a downsampled chain, or a fixed-tap kernel at a resolution chosen from the width, so the taps are bounded on every screen; the blur's shape as a fraction of the frame kept. Replay identical.
